name: TROGGU
description: Troggu (Trogga) is a Swiss Tarot game from the German-speaking Valais. Uses a modified 62-card Tarot deck. 3-8 players. Features bidding (Normal/Solo), Tapp exchange, the unique Fool as highest trump, and Misere when all pass. The secret partner mechanic (calling a trump card) adds intrigue in 7-8 player games.

content.text: Troggu (Trogga) is a Swiss Tarot game from the German-speaking Valais. Uses a modified 62-card Tarot deck. 3-8 players. Features bidding (Normal/Solo), Tapp exchange, the unique Fool as highest trump, and Misere when all pass. The secret partner mechanic (calling a trump card) adds intrigue in 7-8 player games.

Troggu is a Swiss Tarot game from the German-speaking Valais (Upper Wallis), played especially in the Visp area, St. Niklaus, and Grächen. Card game researcher John McLeod places its probable origin in the 18th century; the game's mix of Fool-as-excuse and Fool-as-highest-trump rules suggests a transitional form between older Tarot and modern Tarock. A related game may have reached Belgium in the 18th century, evidenced by Cartes de Suisses decks. Its closest relatives are Tape (Fribourg) and Dappen (Baden). After Troccas, Troggu is the second most played tarot game in Switzerland.
62 cards (78 minus low swords/batons and high cups/coins). 21 trumps + Fool + 40 suit cards. Total 114 pts.
